instruction: Search for 'drip coffee maker' on Amazon.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to search for drip coffee makers on Google Shopping but encountered SSL cert error (NET::ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID). Navigated to Amazon instead, searched 'drip coffee maker', applied color/price/deals filters, scrolled results. Later tried Google Shopping URL but landed on Best Buy. Failed after 50 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Chrome address bar, type URLs, search products on Amazon, use search filters (color, price, deals), scroll through results, interact with web elements
metadata.failure_analysis: Google Shopping inaccessible due to SSL certificate error. Model could not bypass the cert error and tried alternative shopping sites instead. Evaluator expected Google Shopping-specific URL and filter states.
metadata.task_rationale: Extracted the core sub-task the model actually completed successfully: navigating to Amazon and searching for 'drip coffee maker'. The model demonstrated this exact capability in the trajectory (screenshots 10-35). This isolates the search ability from the unavailable Google Shopping requirement.
metadata.explanation: Task requires searching for 'drip coffee maker' on Amazon. Evaluator uses URL pattern matching to verify: (1) the active tab is on amazon.com, and (2) the URL contains 'drip coffee maker' (with flexible character matching for URL encoding like + or %20). Uses official getter active_url_from_accessTree and metric is_expected_url_pattern_match. Both regex patterns must match.

scoring_breakdown.navigation_and_search: 1.0 - URL on amazon.com AND contains drip coffee maker query

llm_judge_reasons: Getter active_url_from_accessTree correctly extracts the active tab URL as a string, which is the right state to verify navigation and search.
Metric is_expected_url_pattern_match correctly receives the rules dict and accesses rules['expected'] to get the pattern list. All patterns must match for score=1.0, which enforces both requirements.
Pattern 'amazon\.com' correctly verifies the user navigated to Amazon.
Pattern 'drip.coffee.maker' correctly verifies the search query is present in the URL. The regex '.' wildcard appropriately handles URL-encoded separators (+, %20, -, etc.).
Complete coverage: both instruction requirements (navigate to Amazon + search for 'drip coffee maker') are verified by the two URL patterns.
Data flow is correct: getter returns string URL -> metric does regex search on all patterns -> returns 1.0 only if all match.
